title: Page result
description: One line of runs/<run_id>/pages.jsonl. Rows are sorted by page_id in codepoint order, independent of the order work completed (SC-003).

levelMetrics.description: Metrics at one normalisation level. Edit counts and denominators are kept so that corpus aggregation is a sum, never an average of averages. Neither denominator can be zero, and that is a guarantee made upstream by validate, not a hope: see the minimums below.

cer.description: char_edits / ref_chars. Unbounded above: a runaway prediction can exceed 1.

ref_chars.description: Never 0. validate rejects any non-probe reference that normalises to empty at ANY of the three levels — a reference of nothing but punctuation empties at skeleton, one of nothing but diacritics empties at diacritic_insensitive — so no CER denominator can be zero (research R-009).

ref_words.description: Never 0, and this follows from ref_chars: tokens are runs of non-whitespace after normalisation, so a normalised reference that is non-empty contains at least one token. The same upstream check protects both denominators.

outcome.description: The [UNREADABLE] contract classification (FR-010). correct_refusal and hallucination are probe pages and carry no metrics. false_refusal is a legible page transcribed as the marker: it carries metrics AND is counted separately.

metrics.description: Absent when outcome is correct_refusal or hallucination — a probe page has no reference text to measure distance against.

order.description: Reading-order measurements (FR-012). Computed at strict level over non-empty lines, matched on skeleton similarity.

order_corrected_cer.description: Strict CER after matched prediction lines are re-emitted in reference order. Recognition quality with sequencing removed.

reading_order_accuracy.description: Fraction of matched line pairs whose relative order agrees between reference and prediction. null — never 1.0 — when fewer than two lines matched, and excluded from the aggregate in that case.

flags.description: Sorted. Flagged pages stay in the aggregate; the flag tells a reader where an error rate came from (FR-011).

$comment: All floats are serialised at 6 decimal places through one shared helper, so two runs on identical inputs produce byte-identical files (SC-003).
